extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff; counsel handling reciprocal discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a state authority has disciplined an attorney, including notice/response requirements, the ability to oppose on enumerated grounds, imposition of identical discipline (public reprimand and probation), enforcement via Order to Show Cause, and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, reciprocal discipline may be imposed when a duly constituted authority of a State has publicly disciplined an attorney; the Office may order discipline identical to that imposed by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director (or designee) may impose the same sanction imposed by the state authority (here: public reprimand and two-year probation). The Final Order here was predicated upon the respondent being publicly reprimanded and subjected to a two-year probationary term by a duly constituted authority of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Opportunity to Respond (40-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be mailed (certified mail in this instance) and delivered; the respondent has a defined 40-day window to assert grounds under 11.24(d)(1). Failure to timely respond is consequential (see 'Effect of no response').

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (reference to 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose the imposition of reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references 11.24(d)(1) as the sole basis for opposing identical reciprocal discipline; the Final Order does not enumerate those grounds but makes clear that a timely response asserting such grounds is required to create a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to file a response (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and public reprimand of Respondent is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not contest within the prescribed period, the OED/Director may conclude there is no genuine issue and impose reciprocal discipline without further factual inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as a disciplinary sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order demonstrates that the USPTO may impose a public reprimand identical to the sanction imposed by the State authority when reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary term specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a two-year probationary period commencing on the date on which this Final Order is signed;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation terms (length and commencement) may mirror the State order; the Order sets a specific start date (signing date) and duration (two years) and ties enforcement procedures to that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the two-year probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any provision of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not impose an additional disciplinary sanction from among the options set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a) for the violations set forth in the Complaint, (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record known to the OED Director, and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure requires issuance, service to the last known address, and a 15-day response period. This provides a defined administrative pathway before recommending additional sanctions to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to USPTO Director for additional sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after consideration of Respondent's response (if any), the OED Director remains of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply during the probationary period, the OED Director shall: (A) deliver to the USPTO Director or his designee: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response to the Order to Show Cause, if any, and (iii) evidence and argument causing the OED Director to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply..., and (B) request that the USPTO Director impose an additional and appropriate disciplinary sanction from among the options set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a) for the violations set forth in the Complaint;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director compiles the record and requests that the USPTO Director impose one of the sanctions enumerated in 11.20(a); this is the escalation step following the Order to Show Cause process.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's ability to pursue independent discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that the USPTO Director additionally disciplines Respondent pursuant to paragraph '3' above, nothing herein shall prevent the OED Director from pursuing independent discipline for the misconduct leading to the imposition of additional discipline pursuant to paragraph '3' above;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director retains authority to pursue separate or additional disciplinary proceedings even after seeking or after the USPTO Director imposes supplemental discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: (Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation ... [template provided])
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires public notice in the Official Gazette using a materially consistent template that summarizes the sanction, jurisdictional basis, and factual findings; the sample notice includes the respondent's practice authorization (e.g., trademark/non-patent matters) and the factual predicate for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and example of Rule 3.4 violation (Fairness to Opposing Party and Counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fifth District Subcommittee found that these acts constituted a violation of Rule 3.4 - Fairness to Opposing Party and Counsel, which precludes a lawyer from threatening to present criminal or disciplinary charges solely to obtain an advantage in a civil matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order gives concrete examples of impermissible conduct: (1) letters threatening to bring criminal perjury charges to resolve civil disputes; (2) asserting one would not report misrepresentations and material omissions to state/governmental agencies in return for payment; (3) threatening to notify regulatory authorities in order to obtain a favorable settlement. Such threats, used solely to obtain advantage in civil matters, violate Rule 3.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24. Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the statutory/regulatory basis for USPTO disciplinary action and notes transparency via FOIA access to disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the OED Director to follow the recordkeeping/publication or other procedural requirements specified in 11.59 (the Order does not restate § 11.59's text but mandates compliance).
